evidence.setup: Python Z-set/bag edge relation with derived self-join path2; 20,000 randomized signed diffs including -2,-1,+1,+2; incremental differential formula compared after every step with full recomputation.
evidence.result: PASS: 20,000 / 20,000 steps matched full recomputation; zero observed mismatches.
evidence.boundary: Synthetic Python oracle; not current ClayCode compiler/runtime.

evidence.setup: Multiple support weight x=2, then apply diff=-1.
evidence.result: Correct multiplicity remains 1; naive set-only deletion makes x absent and is incorrect.

evidence.setup: argmax over scores a=10,b=9,c=8; delete a; compare full selector recomputation with support-only invalidation.
evidence.result: Full recomputation selects b; support-only invalidation retracts a but fails to discover b.

evidence.setup: Data unchanged; selector semantics change from max to min.
evidence.result: Result changes despite data_diff=0, proving selector/plan identity is itself an invalidation dependency.

evidence.setup: 100,000-element global max selector; 2,000 point updates; compare naive full max scan with maintained lazy heap index.
evidence.result: Median naive full scan approximately 1.768707 ms/update; indexed update approximately 0.000147 ms/update; synthetic ratio approximately 12,032x.
evidence.boundary: Intentionally synthetic microbenchmark; ratio must not be projected to Frank/Clay target runtime.

supported_at_current_scope: Signed multiplicity/diff semantics are a viable exact basis for tested differential operators.
Support-only closure is unsound for tested non-monotone selector deletion.
Selector/plan changes require invalidation even with no data delta.
Coherent progress/sealed-epoch knowledge is the leading correctness model for out-of-order logical-time updates.
not_established: Correctness of the full ClayCode compiler/runtime incremental engine
